facts.statement: The species M. validus was named in 1916 based on three complete skulls found in the Chinle Formation of Arizona.
facts.quote: M. validus, once thought to be the type species of Machaeroprosopus, was named in 1916 on the basis of three complete skulls from Chinle Formation, Arizona.

facts.statement: The original skulls of M. validus were lost in the 1950s, leaving only a line drawing from the 1916 description as a visual record.
facts.quote: The skulls have been lost since the 1950s, and a line drawing in the original 1916 description is the only visual record of the specimen.

facts.statement: M. andersoni was described by Maurice G. Mehl in 1922 based on a partial skull holotype.
facts.quote: M. andersoni was first described and named by Maurice G. Mehl in 1922, on the basis of the holotype FMNH UC 396, partial skull.

facts.statement: Specimens of M. andersoni were likely collected from the Bull Canyon Formation in Guadalupe County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: It was probably collected from the Bull Canyon Formation of the Chinle Group or Dockum Group, probably at the Bull Canyon, in the Guadalupe County of New Mexico.

facts.statement: M. buceros was originally named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1881 as Belodon buceros based on a partial skull.
facts.quote: M. buceros was first described and named by Edward Drinker Cope in 1881 as Belodon buceros, on the basis of the holotype AMNH 2318, partial skull.

facts.statement: The holotype of M. buceros was collected from the Norian-aged Chinle Formation in Rio Arriba County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Norian-aged Petrified Forest Member of the Chinle Formation, at the Arroyo Seco drainage, Orphan Mesa in the Rio Arriba County of New Mexico.

facts.statement: M. jablonskiae was described by Parker and Irmis in 2006 based on a posterior skull roof and braincase.
facts.quote: M. jablonskiae was first described and named by William G. Parker and Randall B. Irmis in 2006, on the basis of the holotype PEFO 31207, posterior skull roof and braincase missing the rostrum and palate.

facts.statement: The holotype of M. jablonskiae was collected in September 2002 near Mountain Lion Mesa in Petrified Forest National Park, Arizona.
facts.quote: It was collected in September 2002 from the lower Jim Camp Wash beds, Sonsela Member of the Chinle Formation, at locality PFV 295, near Mountain Lion Mesa in Petrified Forest National Park, Arizona.

facts.statement: The specific name of M. jablonskiae honors Pat Jablonsky, who discovered the only known specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Pat Jablonsky, who discovered the holotype and only known specimen.

facts.statement: M. lottorum was named in 2013 by Axel Hungerbühler, Bill Mueller, Sankar Chatterjee, and Douglas P. Cunningham.
facts.quote: M. lottorum was first described and named by Axel Hungerbühler, Bill Mueller, Sankar Chatterjee and Douglas P. Cunningham in 2013.

facts.statement: M. lottorum is known from two complete skulls housed at Texas Tech University.
facts.quote: It is known from two complete skulls, the holotype TTU-P10076 and the paratype TTU-P10077 housed at Texas Tech University.

facts.statement: Specimens of M. lottorum were collected 13 km south of Post in Garza County, Texas, from the Norian Cooper Canyon Formation.
facts.quote: The skulls were collected at Patricia Site (TTU Vertebrate Paleontology Locality 3870), 13 km South of Post, Garza County of west Texas, from the upper unit of the Norian Cooper Canyon Formation, Dockum Group.

facts.statement: Most species formerly assigned to Machaeroprosopus have been reassigned to the genera Smilosuchus, Rutiodon, or Phytosaurus.
facts.quote: Most species have been reassigned to the genera Smilosuchus, Rutiodon, or Phytosaurus.

facts.statement: The genus name Pseudopalatus is now considered a junior synonym of Machaeroprosopus.
facts.quote: Therefore, the name Pseudopalatus must be considered a junior synonym of Machaeroprosopus, and all species of the former must be reassigned to the latter.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis suggests M. jablonskiae is the most basal species within the group formerly known as Pseudopalatus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis of mystriosuchin phytosaurs performed by Parker and Irmis (2006) found the species to be the most basal species of "Pseudopalatus".

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis indicates M. lottorum is a derived species closely related to Redondasaurus gregorii.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis of mystriosuchin phytosaurs performed by Hungerbühler et al. (2013) found the species to be a derived Machaeroprosopus species, most closely related to the type species of Redondasaurus, "R." gregorii.

facts.statement: Machaeroprosopus was historically considered a doubtful name due to a lack of diagnostic specimens distinguishing it from other phytosaurs.
facts.quote: Thus, Machaeroprosopus was considered to be a nomen dubium or "doubtful name" because of the lack of diagnostic specimens that can support its distinction from other phytosaur genera.

facts.statement: M. jablonskiae is notable for having a well-preserved braincase, a feature rarely found in detail in phytosaur fossils.
facts.quote: Although M. jablonskiae is known from an incomplete specimen, it can be diagnosed by at least one autapomorphy and a unique suite of traits, and it includes a well-preserved braincase, which is rarely preserved or described in detail for most phytosaur specimens.

facts.statement: Machaeroprosopus mccauleyi was described in 1989 based on an incomplete skull missing the front part of the snout.
facts.quote: M. mccauleyi was first described and named by Karen A. Ballew in 1989 as a species of Pseudopalatus, on the basis of the holotype UCMP 126999, an incomplete skull, lacking the anterior half of the rostrum, and probably associated lower jaws.

facts.statement: The species name mccauleyi honors the McCauley couple who owned the land where the holotype was discovered.
facts.quote: The specific name honors John D. McCauley and Mrs. Molly McCauley McLean from Winslow, Arizona, the owners of the land at "Billings Gap" from which the holotype was found.

facts.statement: Machaeroprosopus pristinus was originally named in 1928 based on a nearly complete skull.
facts.quote: M. pristinus was first described and named by Maurice G. Mehl in 1928 as the type species of Pseudopalatus, Pseudopalatus pristinus, on the basis of the holotype MU 525, nearly complete skull.

facts.statement: The holotype of M. pristinus was collected near Adamana, Arizona, from the Norian-aged Upper Petrified Forest Member.
facts.quote: It was collected, from the Norian-aged Upper Petrified Forest Member of the Chinle Formation, near Adamana, Arizona.

facts.statement: Additional skulls and articulated skeletons attributed to M. pristinus have been found in both Arizona and New Mexico.
facts.quote: Additional skulls and postcranial material, some articulated skeletons, from the same member were referred to this species by Colbert (1946) and Long and Murry (1995) from Arizona, and by Lawler (1979), Ballew (1986) and Long and Murry (1995) from New Mexico.

facts.statement: Machaeroprosopus validus was described in 1916 based on a complete skull and two partial skulls found in Coconino County, Arizona.
facts.quote: M. validus was first described and named by Maurice G. Mehl in Mehl et al., in 1916 on the basis of the holotype UW 3807, a complete skull, and the two paratypes UW 3808 and UW 3809, partial skulls, from Norian-aged Upper Petrified Forest Member of the Chinle Formation, Coconino County of Arizona.

facts.statement: Recent research determined that the holotype of the genus Machaeroprosopus is actually M. buceros, not M. validus.
facts.quote: However, a taxonomic revision of Machaeroprosopus, conducted by Parker et al. (in press), revealed that UW 3807 is not the holotype of Machaeroprosopus, while the species Machaeroprosopus buceros is in fact the correct new combination for the type species of the genus.

facts.statement: Machaeroprosopus is classified as a phytosaur from the Late Triassic, belonging to the subfamily Pseudopalatinae.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Triásico Superior, regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Sauropsida unranked_ordo: Archosauria ordo: Phytosauria familia: Phytosauridae subfamilia: Pseudopalatinae

facts.statement: The genus Machaeroprosopus includes multiple species such as M. andersoni, M. buceros, M. jablonskiae, M. lottorum, M. mccauleyi, M. pristinus, and M. validus.
facts.quote: subdivision: M. andersoni Mehl, 1922 M. buceros (Cope, 1881) M. jablonskiae (Parker & Irmis, 2006) M. lottorum Hungerbühler et al., 2013 M. mccauleyi (Ballew, 1989) M. pristinus (Mehl, 1928) M. validus Mehl in Mehl et al., 1916

facts.statement: The genus Pseudopalatus is now considered a junior synonym of Machaeroprosopus, requiring all its species to be reassigned.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, el nombre Pseudopalatus debe ser considerado como un sinónimo más moderno de Machaeroprosopus, y todas las especies del primero deben ser reasignadas a este último.

facts.statement: Machaeroprosopus lived during the Norian to Rhaetian stages of the Late Triassic, between 227.3 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database classifies Machaeroprosopus within the family Parasuchidae and the subfamily Mystriosuchini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mystriosuchini Family: Parasuchidae

facts.statement: Machaeroprosopus is an extinct pseudopalatine phytosaur from the Late Triassic of the southwestern United States.
facts.quote: Machaeroprosopus es un género extinto de fitosáurido pseudopalatino del Triásico Superior del suroeste de Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: A taxonomic revision revealed that the holotype of the genus Machaeroprosopus is the species formerly known as Pseudopalatus buceros, not M. validus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, una revisión taxonómica de Machaeroprosopus, llevada a cabo por Parker et al. (en prensa), reveló que UW 3807, el holotipo de M. validus, no es el holotipo de Machaeroprosopus, mientras que la especie ya nombrada Pseudopalatus buceros tenía la prioridad como la especie tipo del género.
